overall_note: 31 records reviewed via NCBI E-utilities only (no web access). 22 resolved and matched with high confidence (KEEP where the abstract text confirms the claim verbatim). One CONFIRMED citation error: Cochrane CD001431.pub6 decision-aids review — dossier's own flag was correct, first author is Stacey D, not Smith M (Smith M is 3rd of 21 authors). One important overclaim caught: the GBD 2023 IPV paper (S0140-6736(25)02503-6) abstract supports the 18.5 million DALYs figure but contains NO mortality/death count — the dossier's '~145,000 deaths' figure is unsupported by the abstract and should be dropped or independently sourced. Two numeric sub-claims could not be confirmed from abstracts alone even though the parent papers are real: Ellsberg 2015's '58 reviews / 84 interventions' and Bacchus 2024's '19 of 30 primary prevention' — both are absent from the retrieved abstract text (the qualitative claims attached to each ARE supported). Two items (Fawcett 2010 premarital-education meta-analysis DOI, and Charoenwong 2025 Asia-Pacific Social Science Review) could not be resolved at all via PubMed/DOI/title search and are recommended DROP pending author-supplied verifiable sources — both happen to be among the explicitly flagged strict-check items in the review brief (Fawcett's 47-studies/null-result claim). WHO fact-sheet figures (31.6%/840 million, and the 'updated 18 June 2026' fact sheet) could not be confirmed by this tool (WHO pages are not PubMed-indexed and no web access was permitted) and are flagged FIX pending direct URL verification; per the applicable rule they remain in_scope as authoritative guidance despite fetched=false. JAKIM and Malaysia-government items are correctly scoped in the dossier as context-only, non-medical-evidence sources (in_scope=false), consistent with the rule.
